item.title: At least 1 in 4 ex-NFL players who died from 2016 to 2021 had CTE, study finds
item.description: That's a much higher rate than is seen in the general population. CTE is a brain disease linked to repeated blows to the head.

item.title: Multiple people dead, including kids, in shooting and fire at Montana home
item.description: The suspect in the incident later died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, law enforcement said.

item.title: Trump administration's plan to sever Iran's economy until it "stands alone"
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced a new economic plot against Iran and threatened countries that continue to trade with Tehran. CBS News' Aaron Navarro has more.

item.title: Supreme Court will allow citizenship checks on mail-in ballots
item.description: The Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to move forward with citizenship checks on mail-in ballots, ruling states suing the White House over President Trump's executive order don't have the legal right to challenge it. Ed O'Keefe has the latest.

item.title: Supreme Court sides with Trump on mail-in voting, making way for more legal challenges
item.description: The Supreme Court has allowed the Trump administration to implement portions of an order meant to restrict mail-in voting. CBS News' Katrina Kaufman explains the court's legal reasoning and what to expect going forward.

item.title: Rape and murder of toddler in Nepal sparks calls for the death penalty
item.description: Protesters and politicians enraged by the rape and murder of a 3-year-old girl in Nepal are demanding the country institute the death penalty.

item.title: Why the judge in the Lindsay Clancy trial scolded prosecutors for testimony on her faith
item.description: The defense in the Lindsay Clancy trial called for a mistrial after a witness brought up Lindsay Clancy's Catholic faith. The judge did not declare a mistrial, but he reprimanded prosecutors and told the jury to ignore that testimony. Trial lawyer Mark Eiglarsh explains more.

item.title: U.S. Air Force major criminally charged for criticizing Trump
item.description: U.S. Air Force Maj. Jason Watson, who has served for 17 years, now faces rare criminal charges for criticizing President Trump. Watson has been detained twice recently for similar charges. Charlie D'Agata reports

item.title: Firefighters work to contain Hawk Fire near Reno
item.description: Firefighters in Nevada are working to contain the Hawk Fire as more than 20,000 residents are still unable to return home and schools remain closed. Meanwhile, wildfires continue to singe other parts of the western U.S. Jason Allen reports.

item.title: Wife pleads for release of Latin Grammy-winning Cuban musician detained by ICE
item.description: Degnis Bofill, who won a 2022 Latin Grammy, is being held at the Krome Detention Center in Miami-Dade County while his asylum case is pending.

item.title: Iran says it's ready for new U.S. sanctions, has 2-year plan
item.description: Iran's economy minister said the country has been preparing for a long time for the sanctions U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described as the "greatest financial offensive" ever.

item.title: Eye Opener: Hawk Fire continues to rage near Reno
item.description: Firefighters continue to battle the Hawk Fire, a wildfire near Reno, Nevada, as tens of thousands remain unable to return to their homes. Meanwhile, a U.S. Air Force major faces criminal charges for criticizing President Trump. All that and all that matters in today's Eye Opener.

item.title: Can Men Wear Shorts to the Office? | Money Moves with Jill Schlesinger
item.description: It's a career advice episode! Jill and Mark tackle the big questions: Should you follow a great mentor or stay for a bigger paycheck? When does switching fields make sense? And is owning your own business really better than being an employee? Plus: Jill weighs in on appropriate office attire (spoiler: no shorts for men) and Mark wonders whether his wife is spending too much money on accessories.

item.title: Chinese ship caught with banned shark fins in Pacific Ocean
item.description: The ship was among four vessels detained in a surveillance crackdown by 11 Pacific island nations, assisted by the U.S. Coast Guard.

item.title: South Carolina Senate race heads to runoff today
item.description: Darline Graham, the sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, is facing off against Rep. Ralph Norman for the GOP nomination.

item.title: Trump and Kennedy's health industry deals are at risk of vanishing
item.description: The agreements, covering issues like drug pricing, reducing the use of synthetic food dyes, and cutting back on insurance prior authorization rules, were announced with fanfare and touted as victories.

item.title: Tornado in France injures 41 people, damages hundreds of homes
item.description: Winds are estimated to have reached 73 mph.

item.title: Amazon driver strikes 71-year-old man in Northern California gas station in newly released video
item.description: Newly released surveillance video shows an Amazon delivery driver striking a 71-year-old man inside an Elk Grove gas station earlier this year after a dispute over a parking space, officials said.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial judge denies mistrial request, reprimands prosecution
item.description: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony ended abruptly Monday in Plymouth Superior Court when a witness began speaking about religion and the defense unsuccessfully called for a mistrial.

item.title: Body of wife wanted in Worcester, Massachusetts, police officer's death found
item.description: Karen Solomon​, wanted for questioning in the death of her Worcester, Massachusetts, police officer​ husband, has been found dead after a massive search.

item.title: Jared Kushner and Hakeem Jeffries met as midterm elections loom
item.description: The meeting came with Democrats expected to take control of the House in the November elections, which would put Jeffries in line to become the next House speaker.

item.title: Former Stars and Stripes editor says firing was a "real shock"
item.description: Days after his sudden firing by the Pentagon, Erik Slavin, the former editor-in-chief of Stars and Stripes, told CBS News that "time will tell" whether the military newspaper will remain editorially independent.

item.title: Supreme Court allows Trump to implement parts of order restricting mail voting
item.description: The Supreme Court divided 6-3 in granting the Trump administration's request for emergency relief.

item.title: Mike Lindell withholds payment for recount request in Minnesota GOP governor primary
item.description: Mike Lindell is withholding the payment required for a recount and audit of ballots cast in the Republican primary for Minnesota governor, claiming that the Secretary of State's office has proposed an unlawful recount process, according to a statement released by his campaign Monday.

item.title: Trump announces 50% tariffs on Canadian automotive and steel imports
item.description: President Trump said tariffs on Canadian automotive and steel imports will rise to 50% on Jan. 1, 2027, in a social media post.

item.title: New evidence emerges in deadly 1988 Lockerbie bombing, delaying trial
item.description: A federal judge has postponed a trial in the U.S. for a Libyan man charged in the 1988 bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, citing the discovery of new evidence.

item.title: Former Stars and Stripes editor-in-chief says his firing "was a real shock"
item.description: The Pentagon has terminated several staff members of the military newspaper "Stars and Stripes" for alleged insubordination. Former Editor-In-Chief Erik Slavin says he was removed because of an interview he gave to "CBS Sunday Morning" about censorship. Slavin joins "The Takeout" to discuss his removal.

item.title: 8/24: CBS Evening News
item.description: Fast-moving wildfires drive thousands from their homes; Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney asks the judge to declare a mistrial.

item.title: Supreme Court lets Trump's order overhauling mail-in voting take effect for now
item.description: The Supreme Court on Monday allowed President Trump's executive order targeting mail-in voting to take effect while legal challenges play out. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson breaks down the procedural decision.

item.title: Gen Xers fret over Social Security. "I will likely be working in retirement."
item.description: Millions of Generation X Americans expect to depend on Social Security as their main — or only — source of retirement income.
